t: Dataset Join Recommender: a plain-language overview
title: Dataset Join Recommender: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Dataset Join Recommender does and why archives need it. A dataset join recommender looks at two datasets and judges whether they can be combined: do they share a key field, are the types compatible, and would the join actually make sense? It scores every candidate pair and recommends the best joins. Separate tables become combinable knowledge.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Dataset Join Recommender works
title: How the Dataset Join Recommender works
description: Overview: what the Dataset Join Recommender does and why archives need it. Real recommenders score dataset pairs by shared-field detection (name similarity plus value overlap on candidate keys), type compatibility of the join keys, and cardinality estimates (a 1:1 key match joins cleanly; a many:many match warns of explosion). Uniqueness profiling checks whether a candidate key is actually unique, and sample joins on a data slice verify the recommendation before the full join runs. Each recommendation carries its score breakdown.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Dataset Join Recommender works: the deep tour
title: How the Dataset Join Recommender works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Dataset Join Recommender does and why archives need it. Real recommenders score dataset pairs by shared-field detection (name similarity plus value overlap on candidate keys), type compatibility of the join keys, and cardinality estimates (a 1:1 key match joins cleanly; a many:many match warns of explosion). Uniqueness profiling checks whether a candidate key is actually unique, and sample joins on a data slice verify the recommendation before the full join runs. Each recommendation carries its score breakdown. Advanced systems consider multi-column keys, fuzzy keys (names with typos), and semantic keys (different columns, same real-world identifier via the identity graph), and they estimate join result sizes to warn about fan-out. Quality is measured by recommendation precision on known-good join pairs. The limits are coincidental key overlap (two unrelated ID columns) — the recommender requires multi-signal evidence and labels confidence honestly rather than pushing risky joins.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
